And so we see Winter. Based on her interaction with Weiss it makes a bit more sense why Weiss makes the mistakes that she does, I don't know about the rest of you but Weiss has seemed to generally been too focused on 'thinking' about what she'll do next rather then actually do it (much to her detriment during the white trailor or the fight on the train), given how Winter seems to be pushing Weiss for 'perfection' it would make sense that Weiss would develop a bit over-thinking her every move, trying her absolute best to not miss anything as to make her sister happy, but in doing so she just leaves herself too open. Weiss is different from Winter, so she'll need to learn to not let herself be hindered by trying to 'be' Winter if she really wants to fix her MAJOR weakness (at least in 1 on 1 fights). I would also like to point out something a friend pointed out to me, before Winter gets a bit more 'sisterly' she tells the robots to step back, while perhaps nothing my friend at least has some theories about it, I however will go with the far simpler explanation of her trying to put aside her 'work' to be a sister until there's more to suggest otherwise.

Next we have the fight between Winter and Qrow. While very amazing, that fight was easily Qrow's hands down, as we saw his sword started to become a scythe but he stopped it at the end, he didn't go full out because he instead noticed an opportunity to win more 'diplomatically', while I often criticize Ironwood of not being as tactical as Ozpin (YOU DO NOT BRING ROBOTS TO FIGHT AN OPPONENT WHO'S FIRST MOVE YOU KNOW ABOUT WAS UPLOADING A VIRUS INTO YOUR COMPUTERS!), Winter has shown a similar situation with Qrow though not quite as serious a gap. Winter's movements were very precise, and very focuses, Qrow began with the advantage but Winter was holding her own and was slowly gaining ground. It was a VERY enjoyable fight I think being the first time we've seen two 'adults' really go at it, but Qrow still had more to give so I personally am reluctant to say that it was a 'draw' despite what Weiss may say. Also, Qrow winking at Winter as she left the room felt a bit weird to me, I don't know about the rest of you but I don't quite feel comfortable with Qrow and Winter getting together as seems like will be the case. It just feels a bit off to me given how Qrow should be about the age of Ruby and Yang's parents and Yang should be around the same age as Weiss, so it just feels like Winter might be a bit too 'young' for Qrow... But then again Winter did graduate from whatever academy she was in and seems to have become Ironwood's number 2, something he would not have given to someone whom hasn't proven worthy of his trust so perhaps she's quite older than I'm speculating... Qrow having at least some grey hair certainly doesn't help make what I believe to be a big age gap though.

Now onto Cinder. Please note the lines, "The last of the heavy lifting is being taken care of thanks to our clever little friend," which is immediately followed by, "Speaking of which" as she picks up her scroll which shows that she's gained access to Ironwood's scroll, there's a VERY clear implication that whoever this 'friend' is helped with spreading her virus to Ironwood's scroll which means that it probably wasn't Adam as I had thought she meant when I heard the first line originally. If you recall as well, at the end of volume 1 Qrow sent a message to Ozpin telling him "Queen has pawns", and I think we've got a traitor in our midst. While some other possibilities do exist (such as the virus being the little friend, or perhaps Torchwick somehow helping without blowing his cover, potentially even escaping from his cell for periods of time), I can't help but feel like we're being set up for someone to turn out to be a traitor all along. It clearly isn't going to be Ironwood or Ozpin seeing as how they're far too in the spotlight, but potentially everyone else is fair game, Qrow and Winter might be free given how they've only shown up recently so likely haven't had the opportunity for Cinder to convince them to go traitor, but this would leave only the teachers we've met and I personally won't want to become doubtful of any of them quite yet as I like them all. (EDIT: And I JUST realized that the little friend is actually probably Neo, who was put the virus onto Ironwood's scroll during the meeting by hiding what seems to be her illusion based semblance, so potentially false traitor flags might go up as Neo runs around potentially pretending to be other people, after all we didn't see her this episode but know that she is around)

Also, as far as the doubles we got to see from Cinder, the only characters I recognized were Sun and Neptune and Penny with some other girl. It also seems that the background colors behind each student represents what kingdom the students come from, Mistral (where team SSSN comes from) is blue, Vale (team RWBY, JNPR, CFVY, etc.) is green, Atlas is red, and I have no idea what color Vacuo has but if you want to get some info on whatever team was originally on the right the color of their background might help (be aware that originally on the left where Mercury and Emerald were put, it seems Penny and her teammate were there if you look at Cinder's scroll from the back).

Finally, in regards to what I think will come out between the match that this episode ended on, I think that's going to largely depend on if Mercury and Emerald are allowed to go all out. While Cinder would like for them to win, I'm not sure if she wants them to keep some tricks up their sleeves for when she makes her move so if that's the case Mercury and Emerald would be fighting handicapped, and given how their opponents aren't push-overs holding back could cost them the match. But assuming there are no restrictions on them, I think this fight will go to Mercury and Emerald. Mercury is designed to basically be a counter to Yang in almost every way possible, which means that even though Yatsuhashi is incredibly strong it won't be something completely outside of the realm that Mercury can deal with (as otherwise Yang would just absolutely thrash Mercury after taking a few hits), while Mercury may not really be 'tanky' he seems like he'll definitely know how to 'control' a tank, keep them occupied, block attacks, parry others, and generally be able to make sure that Yatsuhashi isn't able to do anything but focus on Mercury, this means that the fight would more likely come down to what would happen between Emerald and Coco (as Mercury would be able to quickly identify Yatsuhashi as who he should go for), as Mercury won't be able to handle both a mini-gun and Yatsuhashi both gunning for him. One advantage for Emerald is that Coco is pretty full of herself (I won't say that it's completely undeserved though), as a result there's no way that Coco is going to pull out her mini-gun first thing, she's going to start off going in for some melee (though will probably give Yatsuhashi some space so she doesn't get caught in his big destructive attacks), this means that if she gets angered and decides to switch tactics later then Mercury will already have Yatsuhashi going at the pace that Mercury sets, leaving Emerald free to give chase to Coco, and once she gets in close Emerald will have the advantage as even if she's a bit of a light-weight she's very.... 'jump', once she's up close with Coco Emerald can get behind her no problem, with Coco's big mini-gun that would leave it basically useless, and for close range Emerald I think would have a bit of an advantage by avoiding Coco's attacks, though given how her bag is a mini-gun it will probably pack a punch, and since Mercury is going to have his hands full with Yatsuhashi I think that Emerald would be on her own against Coco.... Some things that could drastically change the flow of battle though would potentially be Coco's semblance (I imagine Yatsuhashi's has something to do with strenght) but also if you recall Cinder said that she would prepare for tomorrow, and given how she set up the match I wouldn't exactly put it past her to do some very tactical cheating...

But those are just my thoughts!

Looking at @OldRunningMan's comment linking to the classic Idiocracy intro scene, I decided to write up a theory about the future fat of the fats that has been brewing in my mind ever since I starting hanging out in FPH.

The Idiocracy intro cites the oft repeated notion that humans are no longer subject to natural selection ...

1)

There actually still are "natural predators to thin the herd" (though predator maybe isn't the exact right word). Infectious diseases are still in a position that they could wipe out most or all of us. Antibacterial resistance is an example of how microbes are "winning" the war against the microbial eradication strategy of modern medicine. The basic idea, though, is that a child of a fat & unhealthy person is off to a bad start, due to a) epigentics b) nutritional deficiencies and c) damaging environmental effects in the womb (can you imagine being a fetus inside of an obeast? don't tell me that it wouldn't be an awful place to spend your first 9 months of delicate human development).
